nodes.label: Large Power Transformers
nodes.what: High-voltage and generator step-up transformers that connect datacenters and new generation to the transmission system.
nodes.why_matters: A campus cannot be energized, and new generation cannot inject, without these long-lead units. They sit on both the grid path and the behind-the-meter generation path.
relief_levers: standardized specs to cut custom cycle time
nodes.falsify: LPT and GSU quotes return to ~12–18 months with book-to-bill near 1.0 across major OEMs.
nodes.opportunity_on_relief: If transformer delivery shortens, investigate who can actually interconnect and build next: transmission upgrades, switchgear, electrical construction, and remaining generation-headroom deals — not a general 'buy utilities' conclusion.

nodes.label: Grid Interconnection Process
nodes.what: Studies, agreements, and upgrades required to connect new load or new generation to the bulk electric system.
nodes.why_matters: Even financed campuses wait on study results and upgrade assignments. Generation interconnection (what national queue data measure) is not identical to large-load interconnection.
relief_levers: cluster/queue reform that actually cuts time-to-ISA
surplus interconnection / co-location with existing generators
nodes.falsify: Typical large-load and generation interconnection in major AI regions completes in well under two years including required upgrades.
nodes.opportunity_on_relief: If study backlogs clear, the next investigation is whether physical equipment and transmission construction can absorb the newly approved projects.

nodes.label: Heavy-Duty Gas Turbines
nodes.what: Utility-scale gas turbines used to add dispatchable generation or behind-the-meter power for AI campuses.
nodes.why_matters: The main near-term substitute when grid power is slow. Scarcity here limits the relief path, but most of the OEM book is still traditional power, not datacenters.
relief_levers: OEM output ramps that actually ship before 2030
nodes.falsify: New heavy-duty slots available inside ~24 months with diversified OEM capacity and unused 2027–2028 production.
nodes.opportunity_on_relief: If turbine slots open, investigate GSU transformers, gas interconnection, permitting, and whether hyperscalers still prefer grid power on cost/reliability.

nodes.label: Transmission & Substation Upgrades
nodes.what: New or expanded lines, substations, and related civil/electrical work required after an interconnection agreement.
nodes.why_matters: Hundreds of GW already have agreements but are not operating. Post-approval construction can exceed queue time.
nodes.falsify: Capacity with executed interconnection agreements reaches commercial operation on scheduled dates without multi-year post-ISA slips.
nodes.opportunity_on_relief: If transmission construction accelerates, investigate remaining equipment lead times and local permitting of rights-of-way.

nodes.label: Switchgear & Electrical Distribution
nodes.what: Medium- and high-voltage switchgear, breakers, and campus electrical distribution from the substation to IT halls.
nodes.why_matters: Every energized hall needs this gear. Demand is surging, but OEMs are also growing shipments — demand is not automatically scarcity.
nodes.falsify: Switchgear and related electrical gear available on short lead times with book-to-bill near 1.0.
nodes.opportunity_on_relief: If switchgear eases, investigate remaining transformer/GSU bottlenecks and on-site electrical labor to install the gear.

nodes.label: Utility Generation Headroom
nodes.what: Spare generating capacity and energy already connected to the grid that a new AI load can consume without waiting for a new plant.
nodes.why_matters: PJM and other regions forecast large data-center-driven peaks. If existing surplus is thin, new load requires new generation as well as interconnection.
nodes.falsify: Reserve margins and energy prices in AI-heavy zones remain comfortable while GW-scale campuses energize on schedule.
nodes.opportunity_on_relief: If surplus power appears, investigate which sites can actually take it given transformers, interconnection, and local opposition.

nodes.label: Permitting & Siting
nodes.what: Local, state, and federal approvals for datacenters, generation, and transmission, including land use and environmental review.
nodes.why_matters: Can delay projects that already have capital and equipment orders. Evidence of nationwide binding scarcity is thinner than for transformers or turbines.
nodes.falsify: Permitting ceases to appear among top delay causes and typical AI campuses clear entitlements inside one year.
nodes.opportunity_on_relief: If siting clears, investigate whether equipment and interconnection, not paper, become the remaining clock.

nodes.label: Datacenter Shells & Space
nodes.what: Buildings, white space, and 'warm shells' ready to accept IT and power equipment.
nodes.why_matters: Hyperscalers report being short space as well as power. Shells can often be built while waiting on power — so construction scarcity is not automatically the bind.
relief_levers: more general contractors in AI regions
nodes.falsify: Empty energized halls sit unused because construction outruns power and chips.
nodes.opportunity_on_relief: If shells are plentiful, the investigation shifts entirely to energization: transformers, interconnection, and generation.

nodes.label: Liquid Cooling Systems
nodes.what: CDUs, manifolds, coolants, and heat-rejection systems required by high-density AI racks.
nodes.why_matters: AI power density pulls liquid cooling. Strong vendor demand is not the same as a system-wide shortage that stops campuses from energizing.
nodes.falsify: Air-cooled halls deploy latest AI racks at target density, or liquid-cooling lead times fall to ordinary HVAC ranges.
nodes.opportunity_on_relief: If cooling hardware is easy, investigate facility heat rejection, water constraints where still used, and electrical gear that liquid-cooled halls still require.

nodes.label: AI Accelerators
nodes.what: GPUs and custom AI accelerators that populate energized halls. Packaging/HBM constraints are covered in the AI Accelerator X-Ray.
nodes.why_matters: Compute is the demand driver. It is included here to test whether chips still bind datacenter expansion. Current hyperscaler testimony says power and space bind first.
nodes.falsify: Hyperscalers report idle energized halls waiting on GPUs as the dominant delay.
nodes.opportunity_on_relief: If chips flood into already-powered halls, investigate networking (see AI Networking X-Ray) and power/cooling density inside those halls.
